condition: progressive atrophic facial acne scarring on both cheeks refractory to 3 months of oral antibiotics
level_rationale: Ongoing formation of new indented scars on both cheeks in a 23-year-old with dark brown skin despite completing a 3-month course of prescribed oral antibiotics indicates systemic-antibiotic-refractory scarring disease warranting dermatologist evaluation for specialist systemic therapy and scar management, whereas mild dry skin on both cheeks after completing oral antibiotics without active scarring or inflammatory lesions requires only self-care moisturization.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is 23 years old with dark brown skin
Completed 3 months of prescribed oral antibiotics
Still develops new indented or sunken skin scars on both cheeks

everyday_sources.evidence: The cheeks were the most commonly involved site, affecting 131 participants (87.3%), followed by the forehead in 57 (38.0%).
everyday_sources.adaptation: Combined cheek site distribution in young adults with depressed/atrophic facial scars into plain everyday expression 'new sunken skin scars on both cheeks' without naming the underlying diagnosis.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain darker-skin young-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + unsourced hygiene causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact cheek lesion severity control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 23 with dark brown skin, completed 3 months of prescribed oral antibiotics, and ongoing formation of new indented/sunken cheek scars) with an exact 15-vs-15 word span swap and 8 shared leading plus 8 shared trailing tokens. Swapping only atomic fact f3 while keeping 'on both cheeks' unchanged shifts care from dermatologist referral (level 3) to self-care moisturization (level 1) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
